questions.stem_text:
Suppose that an expansionary fiscal policy leads to a large increase in real output and a
small increase in the price level. From this it can be inferred that

options.A: inflation had already impacted the economy before the fiscal stimulus.
options.B: the economy initially had some unemployed resources.

questions.answer_explanation: Correct option: B - the economy initially had some unemployed resources.

questions.stem_text:
Suppose a nation is experiencing an annual budget surplus and uses some of this surplus to
pay down part of the national debt. One potential side effect of this policy would be

options.A: increase interest rates and throw the economy into a recession.
options.B: increase interest rates and depreciate the nation's currency.
options.C: decrease interest rates and risk an inflationary period.
options.D: decrease interest rates and throw the economy into a recession.

questions.answer_explanation: Correct option: C - decrease interest rates and risk an inflationary period.

options.A: the price of a good divided by its marginal utility.
options.B: the marginal utility of the good divided by its price.
options.C: the total utility of the good.
options.D: the difference between the consumer's value and the market price.

questions.answer_explanation: Correct option: D - the difference between the consumer's value and the market price.

options.B: a monopoly sells to two different types of consumers
options.C: a monopoly buys from a monopsony
options.D: a monopolist sells two different types of goods

questions.answer_explanation: Correct option: A - a monopsony buys from a monopoly
